correctness.rationale: arXiv:2610.04317v1, Lemma 3.1 identifies the polynomial contraction quotient with the corresponding split-algebra quotient and says their submodules coincide; Lemma 3.2 proves that quotient is V direct-sum V. Since the split algebra is End_K(V), Schur's commutant is K. Coordinate projections classify every simple submodule of V direct-sum V by a unique K-projective point. The correspondence theorem then gives the complete ideal interval. Distinct projective lines intersect in zero and span K^2. K is infinite because finite center plus central finiteness would make D a finite division ring and therefore commutative.

value.rationale: The projective-line interval is a natural structural invariant of the recent universal counterexample, not an arbitrary slice. It completely resolves the local overideal geometry: minimal composition length, infinitely many maximal overideals, and exact pairwise intersections/sums. This sharpens the original maximality question and quantitatively complements the older semi-maximality theorem, making the witness easier to reuse in module- and ideal-theoretic arguments.
